paper_title: Adapting Whisper for Regional Dialects Enhancing Public Services for   Vulnerable Populations in the United Kingdom
caption: Difference in average word error rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 after cumulative automated optimisation steps.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 after applying cumulative automated optimisation steps, comparing two fine-tuned models: NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars). The vertical axis lists the optimisations applied, ordered from top to bottom as: Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates. The horizontal axis represents the difference in average WER, ranging from 0.000 to approximately 0.0034, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001, and is scaled linearly. Each optimisation step has two corresponding horizontal bars, one for each model, with the exact WER difference values labeled at the end of each bar. For the "Normalised" step, the NESAC model shows a difference of 0.00334, while the SESHA model shows 0.00323. For "Add Spacing", the values are 0.00319 (NESAC) and 0.00344 (SESHA). For "Remove Spacing", the values are 0.00311 (NESAC) and 0.00306 (SESHA). For "Americanisms", the values are 0.00299 (NESAC) and 0.00302 (SESHA). For "Dates", the values are 0.00257 (NESAC) and 0.00228 (SESHA). The bars are arranged in descending order of optimisation steps, and the chart visually compares the performance of the two models across these steps, with the SESHA model generally showing slightly lower WER differences (better performance) in most cases, except for "Add Spacing" and "Normalised" where NESAC performs slightly better. The legend at the bottom indicates the model associated with each bar color.
